name: IN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+15 partisan lean in a favorable Republican environment
Baird's lopsided fundraising edge ($582k vs $54k) plus $537k in outside support
Prediction markets price roughly 94% for the Republican incumbent
No polls or expert ratings show any sign of a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Baird's incumbency, and a ten-to-one fundraising gap leave Cox without a visible path, and prediction markets agree the seat is not in play. Every available signal points to a comfortable Republican hold in the mid-to-high teens.
model.watch: A late-breaking scandal or an unusually large national wave against Republicans could narrow the margin, though an outright upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 4th District is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about fifteen points to the right. Jim Baird, the incumbent, is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. His campaign has raised roughly $582,000 and drawn more than $537,000 in outside support, while Democrat Drew Cox has raised about $54,000 with modest cash on hand. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Baird roughly a 94 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals point the same direction: the district's lean, the incumbent's advantage, and a favorable environment for Republicans in Indiana all favor Baird. Cox would need an unusually large swing to contend, and nothing in the fundraising or spending picture suggests one is forming. The forecast expects Baird to win by a wide margin, in the mid-to-high teens, consistent with recent Republican performance here.
